title: The red-run check strips every wrapper form before it reads the lead word, and its tests cover each wrapper
why: Wrapped mutant lines still pass, and no test turns red if a wrapper form is dropped.
note: After #1728 lands. Three non-blocking findings from #1728's round 2 reviewer (sonnet): (1) lint/check_red_run.py lines 20-22: the docstring omits `#`, curly quotes and the underscore rule, and says 26 where the record says 15 to 26. (2) lead_word strips an outer underscore last, so `_**mutant**_`, `_(none)_`, `~mutant~`, `> mutant` and `1) mutant` pass, and the record's limits do not list them. (3) lint/test_check_red_run.py lines 66-85: no test uses a backtick, `{` or `<` wrapper, or `**mutant**`. Second follow-up on this check tonight (after red-run-first-word-limits). Filed from lane notes-fix-large-3, 20:23 CST Nov 7 (decision cull-rules). Doing in lane notes-fix-large-3 (coordinator 20:24 CST): one normalising function for the red-run label, with a table-driven test; branch red-run-wrapper-tail stacked on #1728.
